'''Tyler Lee-Deon Davis''' (born May 22, 1997) is an American-Puerto Rican professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Osos de Manatí]] of the [[Baloncesto Superior Nacional]] (BSN). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Texas A&M Aggies men's basketball|Texas A&M Aggies]].<ref>[http://www.houstonchronicle.com/sports/aggies/amp/Tyler-Davis-the-one-constant-for-Texas-A-M-12516427.php Tyler Davis has been the one constant for the A&M basketball team]</ref> He also represents the senior [[Puerto Rico national basketball team|Puerto Rican national basketball team]] in international [[national team]] competitions. Standing at a height of {{height|ft=6|in=11}}, he plays at the [[Center (basketball)|center]] position.<ref name='PUR'>[http://www.fiba.basketball/americup/2017/news/tyler-davis-joins-puerto-rico-basketball-family Tyler Davis joins Puerto Rico basketball family]</ref>

==College career==
As a freshman, Davis averaged 11.3 points and 6.2 rebounds per game, joining [[Admon Gilder]] and [[D. J. Hogg]] on a team that reached the Sweet 16.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Baby |first1=Ben |title=Three former D-FW area standouts who will be 'a major factor' for Texas A&M men's basketball |url=https://www.dallasnews.com/sports/texas-am-aggies/2016/11/11/three-former-d-fw-area-standouts-who-will-be-a-major-factor-for-texas-am-men-s-basketball/ |accessdate=February 7, 2020 |work=[[Dallas Morning News]] |date=November 11, 2016}}</ref> As a sophomore, Davis was a second-team All-[[Southeastern Conference|SEC]] player. Between his sophomore and junior season Davis slimmed down to better compete in SEC play. He led the team in scoring as a junior with 14.9 points per game while finishing second in rebounding behind [[Robert Williams III|Robert Williams]] with 8.9 rebounds per game. Following the season, he declared for the NBA draft.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Sayles |first1=Damon |title=Tyler Davis declares for the NBA Draft |url=https://247sports.com/college/texas-am/Article/Texas-AM-basketball-Tyler-Davis-declares-for-the-NBA-Draft-116607373/ |accessdate=June 25, 2018 |work=247sports |date=March 29, 2018}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Oklahoma City Thunder (2018)===
After going undrafted in the [[2018 NBA draft]], Davis joined the [[Brooklyn Nets]] for NBA Summer League play.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Lewis |first1=Brian |title=Surprising Nets connections run deep for first-round draft pick |url=https://nypost.com/2018/06/23/surprising-nets-connections-run-deep-for-first-round-draft-pick/ |accessdate=June 25, 2018 |work=[[New York Post]] |date=June 23, 2018}}</ref> On August 13, 2018, the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] signed Davis to a [[two-way contract]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Thunder Signs Tyler Davis to Two-Way Contract |url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/release-davis-180813 |website=NBA.com |accessdate=August 13, 2018 |date=August 13, 2018}}</ref> Davis made his NBA debut on November 28, 2018, against the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]], playing one minute and grabbing a rebound.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/d/davisty01/gamelog/2019|title=Tyler Davis 2018–19 Game Log|website=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=December 4, 2018}}</ref> On December 28, 2018, Davis was waived by the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Thunder Waives Tyler Davis|url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/davis-181227|date=December 27, 2018|website=NBA.com|accessdate=December 27, 2018}}</ref> He averaged 17.2 points and 11.5 rebounds per game for the [[Oklahoma City Blue]].

===Oklahoma City Blue (2019–2020)===
Davis was re-acquired by the Blue in a trade with the [[Agua Caliente Clippers]] on November 29, 2019.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Mussatto |first1=Joe |title=Oklahoma City Blue acquires center Tyler Davis |url=https://oklahoman.com/article/5648539/oklahoma-city-blue-acquires-center-tyler-davis |accessdate=July 15, 2020 |work=[[The Oklahoman]] |date=November 29, 2019}}</ref>

===Jeonju KCC Egis (2020–2021)===
On July 15, 2020, he signed with [[Jeonju KCC Egis]] of the [[Korean Basketball League]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Carchia |first1=Emiliano |title=Tyler Davis signs in South Korea with KCC Egis |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/tyler-davis-signs-in-south-korea-with-kcc-egis/ |website=Sportando |accessdate=July 15, 2020 |date=July 15, 2020}}</ref>

===Mexico City Capitanes (2021–2022)===
On October 22, 2021, Davis signed with the [[Mexico City Capitanes]] of the [[NBA G League]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Capitanes begin to announce 2021–22 roster|url=https://capitanes.gleague.nba.com/news/capitanes-begin-to-announce-2021-22-roster/|website=NBA.com|date=October 22, 2021|access-date=October 23, 2021}}</ref> Davis was then later waived by the Capitanes after appearing in 10 games and averaged 11.9 points, 8.5 rebounds, 2.0 assists, and 1.6 blocks per game.<ref name="legends" />

===Texas Legends (2022)===
On January 11, 2022, Davis cleared waivers and was acquired by the [[Texas Legends]].<ref name="legends">{{cite web|title=Legends Acquire Tyler Davis|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/legends-acquire-tyler-davis/n-5780684|website=OurSportsCentral.com|date=January 11, 2022|access-date=January 16, 2022}}</ref> However, he was waived on February 9 after a season-ending injury.<ref>{{cite web|title=2021-2022 Texas Legends Transactions History|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/dleague/teams/Texas-Legends/32/Transaction_History/2022|website=RealGM.com|access-date=March 29, 2022}}</ref>

===Osos de Manatí (2024)===
In February 2024, Davis joined the [[Osos de Manatí]] of the [[Baloncesto Superior Nacional]] (BSN).<ref>{{cite web |title=TYLER DAVIS REAPARECE Y ESTARÁ CON OSOS DE MANATÍ DESDE EL ARRANQUE DEL BSN |url=https://canchalatina.com/2024/02/17/tyler-davis-reaparece-y-estara-con-osos-de-manati-desde-el-arranque-del-bsn/ |website=CANCHA LATINA |access-date=December 4, 2024 |date=February 17, 2024}}</ref> 

In July 2024, Davis signed with the [[Busan KCC Egis]] of the [[Korean Basketball League]].<ref>{{cite web |title='추억의 괴물용병'타일러 데이비스, KCC 재입단한다…NBA 역대급 경력자도 KCC와 계약 임박 |url=https://www.chosun.com/sports/basketball/2024/07/22/H5G7CGHWOSMA7F7RV5LRGYGHRA/ |website=스포츠조선 |access-date=December 4, 2024 |date=July 22, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title="계약서 받아놨다" KCC가 '양치기 소년' 타일러 데이비스 입단 확신하는 이유…NBA 경력자 먼로는 막판 조율 남아 |url=https://www.chosun.com/sports/basketball/2024/07/26/7BRC5YQWHZEK75TB5SVAFFN3LA/ |website=스포츠조선 |access-date=December 4, 2024 |date=July 26, 2024}}</ref> On October 15, he was replaced by [[Leon Williams (basketball, born 1986)|Leon Williams]].<ref>{{cite web |author1=이의진 |title=프로농구 디펜딩 챔피언 KCC, 개막 직전 악재…데이비스 이탈 |url=https://www.yna.co.kr/view/AKR20241015121300007 |website=연합뉴스 |access-date=December 4, 2024 |date=October 15, 2024}}</ref>

==National team career==
Davis represented the [[Puerto Rico national basketball team|Puerto Rican national team]] at the [[2017 FIBA AmeriCup]].<ref>[https://247sports.com/college/texas-am/Article/Texas-AM-basketball-Junior-Tyler-Davis-is-leaner-stronger-and-focused-110163969/ New and improved Tyler Davis: 'I'm in the best shape of my life']</ref> Davis averaged 12.3 points, 6.7 rebounds and 1.7 assists per game in the tournament.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20180125134720/https://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/player/p/pid/100239246/sid/8115/tid/349/_/2017_FIBA_AmeriCup/index.html Tyler Davis's profile | 2017 FIBA AmeriCup]</ref>
